question: Should OpenClaw make AI-safety telemetry a stable core capability that includes durable shared-state history and a public plugin emission/permission contract, or should the work be narrowed to existing diagnostics seams and optional plugin-owned extensions?
rationale: The branch changes core product scope, persistent data behavior, Gateway methods, and the plugin SDK contract; code review cannot determine the intended long-term ownership, privacy posture, or compatibility promise.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow stable core contract
options.body: Define the supported event families, retention/redaction policy, plugin permission semantics, and upgrade behavior, then require current-head end-to-end proof before merging.

options.title: Keep it internal to diagnostics first
options.body: Retain only narrowly justified core diagnostics emitters and exporter wiring while deferring public plugin emission, persistence, and operator UI until their contracts are separately approved.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Close or defer the broad implementation until an owner-sponsored design establishes why this scope belongs in core rather than plugins or ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow stable core contract
recommendation.body: Define the supported event families, retention/redaction policy, plugin permission semantics, and upgrade behavior, then require current-head end-to-end proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This author has assembled the current cross-cutting design and is the clearest available routing contact in the supplied history; an official diagnostics/plugin owner should make the final decision.
